issues.body:
## Why

In `etl/manager_similarity_flow.py:27-47`, the function `ensure_manager_similarity_table(conn)` executes table creation DDL only when `isinstance(conn, sqlite3.Connection)`.

When executed against a PostgreSQL connection, `ensure_manager_similarity_table(conn)` executes no statements and provides no fallback or table verification. This inconsistency contrasts with all other table ensure functions across the codebase (such as `etl/conviction_flow.py`, `alerts/db.py`, and `etl/activism_detection.py`), which provide PostgreSQL DDL branches.

## Scope

- Implement PostgreSQL DDL execution in `ensure_manager_similarity_table()` in `etl/manager_similarity_flow.py:27-47` matching dialect patterns used across `etl/`.
- Add test coverage in `tests/test_manager_similarity_flow.py` verifying table creation DDL execution on PostgreSQL connections.

## Implementation Notes

- Mirror the PostgreSQL table creation schema in `etl/conviction_flow.py` using `BIGINT`, `TIMESTAMPTZ`, and `FLOAT` types.
- Ensure idempotent execution using `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS manager_similarity (...)`.

## Non-Goals

- Modifying similarity computation algorithms or vector embedding distance metrics.
- Adding scaffold-only stubs, mocks, or empty bypass functions without wiring up the real implementation does NOT count as done and constitutes a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add PostgreSQL dialect DDL branch to function `ensure_manager_similarity_table()` in `etl/manager_similarity_flow.py`.
- [ ] Add test cases in `tests/test_manager_similarity_flow.py` asserting PostgreSQL DDL executes on non-SQLite connection instances.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `pytest tests/test_manager_similarity_flow.py` executes without errors.
- Calling `ensure_manager_similarity_table(pg_conn)` on a PostgreSQL mock connection executes DDL creating table `manager_similarity`.
- Verification gate: deliberately break the implementation by omitting PostgreSQL handling in `etl/manager_similarity_flow.py` and verify `pytest tests/test_manager_similarity_flow.py` fails.
issues.title: fix(etl): implement Postgres schema check in ensure_manager_similarity_table

issues.body:
## Why

In `adapters/prices.py:231-245`, the method `close_on_or_before(symbol, on)` evaluates `needs_refresh = not window or max(window) < on` to determine whether an external market data fetch is required.

When requesting market prices for a non-trading date (such as a weekend Saturday or Sunday), `max(window) < on` remains True even after fetching because markets are closed on `on`. Because `window` contains Friday's quote (non-empty), `(symbol, on)` is never added to `self._missing`. On subsequent calls for the same symbol and weekend date, `needs_refresh` evaluates to True again, triggering redundant external HTTP network requests on every invocation.

## Scope

- Update `close_on_or_before()` in `adapters/prices.py:231-245` to record evaluated `(symbol, on)` dates in a refreshed/checked set once a lookup window has been queried.
- Add unit test coverage in `tests/test_adapter_base.py` asserting that repeated calls to `close_on_or_before()` for non-trading weekend dates do not trigger duplicate network fetches.

## Implementation Notes

- Track queried date windows using `self._checked_dates: set[tuple[str, date]] = set()`.
- If `(symbol, on)` has already been evaluated and the cache contains the latest available quote before `on`, skip redundant network calls.

## Non-Goals

- Modifying external market data provider endpoints or rate limiter throttling logic.
- Adding scaffold-only stubs, mocks, or empty bypass functions without wiring up the real implementation does NOT count as done and constitutes a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Implement checked date caching in method `close_on_or_before()` in `adapters/prices.py` to prevent redundant network fetches on non-trading dates.
- [ ] Add unit test in `tests/test_adapter_base.py` verifying that multiple lookups for weekend dates invoke the mock provider exactly once.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `pytest tests/test_adapter_base.py` executes without errors.
- Querying `close_on_or_before("AAPL", saturday_date)` multiple times results in exactly 1 call to the underlying provider fetch method.
- Verification gate: deliberately break the implementation by removing the checked date cache in `adapters/prices.py` and verify `pytest tests/test_adapter_base.py` fails on redundant call assertions.
issues.title: fix(prices): eliminate redundant HTTP requests for weekend and holiday dates in PriceAdapter

issues.body:
## Why

In `api/activism.py:195, 255, 365, 432, 515`, query functions (`query_activism_filings`, `query_activism_events`, `query_active_campaigns`, `query_activism_timeline`, `query_manager_campaigns`) execute SQL containing `LEFT JOIN managers m ON m.manager_id = ...`.

In SQLite databases where table `managers` defines primary key column `id` (standard across local SQLite schemas), executing any of these activism queries raises `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column: m.manager_id`, breaking activism API endpoints in local development and offline inspection workflows.

## Scope

- Resolve the manager table join column dynamically in `api/activism.py:195, 255, 365, 432, 515` using dialect helper `manager_id_column(conn)` or `resolve_manager_id_column(conn)`.
- Add test coverage in `tests/test_activism_dialect_portability.py` executing activism queries against SQLite databases where table `managers` has column `id`.

## Implementation Notes

- Use `manager_id_column(conn)` or `resolve_manager_id_column(conn)` to dynamically format `LEFT JOIN managers m ON m.{manager_col} = ...`.
- Ensure parameter bindings remain parameterized and only the validated column identifier is formatted into the SQL clause.

## Non-Goals

- Changing activism endpoint schemas or modifying PostgreSQL schema definitions.
- Adding scaffold-only stubs, mocks, or empty bypass functions without wiring up the real implementation does NOT count as done and constitutes a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update SQL query templates in `api/activism.py` to resolve dialect-specific manager column names in table joins.
- [ ] Add regression tests in `tests/test_activism_dialect_portability.py` executing activism queries against SQLite connections with `id` PK columns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `pytest tests/test_activism_dialect_portability.py` executes without errors.
- Query functions in `api/activism.py` return valid records when queried against SQLite schemas without raising `OperationalError`.
- Verification gate: deliberately break the implementation by hardcoding `m.manager_id` in `api/activism.py` joins and verify `pytest tests/test_activism_dialect_portability.py` fails on SQLite schemas.
issues.title: fix(api-activism): resolve SQLite column error for managers table join in activism queries

issues.body:
## Why

In `alerts/models.py:33-35`, the rule condition `similar_manager_count_gte` is listed in `_NUMERIC_CONDITION_BOUNDS` as a floating-point number with range `(1.0, None)`, rather than in `_INTEGER_CONDITION_KEYS` alongside `manager_count_gte` and `news_count_gt`.

Because `similar_manager_count_gte` represents a discrete count of similar investment managers, fractional values such as `2.5` should be rejected during validation. Furthermore, in `alerts/engine.py:100-105`, event payload matching evaluates `_as_int(payload.get("similar_manager_count"))` while comparing against `_as_float(expected)`.

## Scope

- Move `similar_manager_count_gte` to `_INTEGER_CONDITION_KEYS` in `alerts/models.py:33-35` and set integer lower bound `similar_manager_count_gte: (1, None)`.
- Update threshold extraction in function `evaluate_rule()` in `alerts/engine.py:100-105` to parse discrete count thresholds.
- Add test cases in `tests/test_alert_engine.py` verifying that fractional values for `similar_manager_count_gte` raise validation errors.

## Implementation Notes

- In `alerts/models.py`, add `"similar_manager_count_gte"` to `_INTEGER_CONDITION_KEYS` and `_INTEGER_CONDITION_BOUNDS = {"similar_manager_count_gte": (1, None)}`.
- In `alerts/engine.py`, ensure count condition evaluation checks integer thresholds consistently across event evaluation flows.

## Non-Goals

- Modifying threshold bounds for continuous financial metrics such as `value_usd_gt` or `pct_change_gte`.
- Adding scaffold-only stubs, mocks, or empty bypass functions without wiring up the real implementation does NOT count as done and constitutes a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Relocate `similar_manager_count_gte` to integer condition collections in `alerts/models.py`.
- [ ] Align rule evaluation in function `evaluate_rule()` in `alerts/engine.py` to parse count thresholds as integers.
- [ ] Add test cases in `tests/test_alert_engine.py` validating that fractional threshold configurations are rejected with validation errors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `pytest tests/test_alert_engine.py` executes without errors.
- Constructing `AlertRuleCreate(name="test", event_type="similarity_cluster", conditions={"similar_manager_count_gte": 2.5})` raises `ValueError`.
- Verification gate: deliberately break the implementation by allowing float inputs for `similar_manager_count_gte` in `alerts/models.py` and verify `pytest tests/test_alert_engine.py` fails.
issues.title: fix(alerts): enforce integer validation for similar_manager_count_gte rule condition

issues.body:
## Why

In `ui/upload.py:43-44`, the function `_load_managers(conn)` executes SQL `SELECT manager_id, name FROM managers ORDER BY name ASC`.

On SQLite database instances created via `_ensure_manager_table()` or `scripts/seed_managers.py`, the primary key column on table `managers` is named `id`, not `manager_id`. Executing `_load_managers(conn)` raises `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column: manager_id`, which is caught by the exception block, causing `_load_managers(conn)` to silently return an empty list `[]` and rendering the manager selector empty during manual filing uploads.

## Scope

- Update `_load_managers()` in `ui/upload.py:43-44` to resolve the manager primary key column dynamically using `resolve_manager_id_column(conn)` from `adapters.base`.
- Add test coverage in `tests/test_upload.py` ensuring `_load_managers()` successfully loads manager records from SQLite databases with `id` column schemas.

## Implementation Notes

- Use `from adapters.base import resolve_manager_id_column` in `ui/upload.py` to dynamically construct `SELECT {id_col}, name FROM managers ORDER BY name ASC`.
- Verify exception handling logs unexpected database errors while keeping graceful empty list fallbacks for uninitialized databases.

## Non-Goals

- Refactoring CSV or PDF parsing pipelines in `ui/upload.py`.
- Adding scaffold-only stubs, mocks, or empty bypass functions without wiring up the real implementation does NOT count as done and constitutes a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Import `resolve_manager_id_column` and update SQL column resolution in function `_load_managers()` in `ui/upload.py`.
- [ ] Add regression test in `tests/test_upload.py` verifying `_load_managers()` queries SQLite tables configured with `id` primary keys.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `pytest tests/test_upload.py` executes without errors.
- Calling `_load_managers(conn)` on an SQLite connection containing table `managers(id, name)` returns populated `[(1, "Manager Name")]` rows.
- Verification gate: deliberately break the implementation by querying hardcoded `SELECT manager_id, name FROM managers` in `ui/upload.py` and confirm `pytest tests/test_upload.py` fails with `OperationalError`.
issues.title: fix(upload-ui): resolve manager_id column dialect error in upload manager loader

issues.body:
## Why

In `ui/alerts.py:75-80`, the helper function `_load_managers(api_url)` queries `GET /managers` and filters the returned items using `if item.get("id") is not None and item.get("name")` to extract `(int(item["id"]), str(item["name"]))`.

The API endpoint `GET /managers` (defined in `api/managers.py:48-62`) returns manager entities serialized with field name `manager_id`, not `id`. As a result, `item.get("id")` is always `None`, causing `_load_managers()` to discard all managers and return an empty list `[]`. Consequently, the manager selector dropdown in the alert creation and subscription interface remains completely empty.

## Scope

- Update `_load_managers()` in `ui/alerts.py:75-80` to retrieve the manager identifier via `item.get("manager_id") or item.get("id")`.
- Add test coverage in `tests/test_ui_alerts.py` to verify that `_load_managers()` parses manager dictionaries containing `manager_id`.

## Implementation Notes

- In `ui/alerts.py`, support both `item.get("manager_id")` and `item.get("id")` to maintain backward and forward compatibility with various backend manager schemas.
- Ensure manager integer conversion handles valid string or integer IDs safely.

## Non-Goals

- Modifying alert channel notifications or altering alert rule dispatch logic in `alerts/engine.py`.
- Adding scaffold-only stubs, mocks, or empty bypass functions without wiring up the real implementation does NOT count as done and constitutes a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update manager ID resolution in function `_load_managers()` in `ui/alerts.py` to accept `manager_id` keys from API payloads.
- [ ] Add regression test in `tests/test_ui_alerts.py` asserting `_load_managers()` returns manager ID and name tuples when given `manager_id` responses.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `pytest tests/test_ui_alerts.py` executes without errors.
- Invoking `_load_managers()` with API payload `[{"manager_id": 1, "name": "Elliott"}]` returns `[(1, "Elliott")]`.
- Verification gate: deliberately break the implementation by requiring `item["id"]` in `ui/alerts.py` and confirm `pytest tests/test_ui_alerts.py` fails.
issues.title: fix(alerts-ui): fix manager selector empty list caused by manager_id key mismatch

issues.body:
## Why

In `ui/dashboard.py:50-55`, the helper function `load_delta(engine)` executes SQL `SELECT filed as date, COUNT(*) AS filings FROM holdings GROUP BY filed ORDER BY filed`.

The `holdings` table schema does not possess a column named `filed` (filing dates are stored in `filings.filed_date` or as timestamp metadata in `holdings.knowledge_time` / `holdings.created_at`). When a user accesses the dashboard and expands the `Historical Filing Trend` section in `ui/dashboard.py:1184`, the database query raises `pandas.errors.DatabaseError: Execution failed on sql ...: no such column: filed`, causing the Streamlit application to crash at runtime.

## Scope

- Update the SQL query in function `load_delta()` in `ui/dashboard.py:50-55` to query `filings.filed_date` from the `filings` table (or join `holdings` to `filings` on `filing_id` when grouping by filing date).
- Add regression testing in `tests/test_dashboard.py` verifying that `load_delta()` executes successfully against database engines with valid filing records.

## Implementation Notes

- In `ui/dashboard.py`, `load_delta(engine)` can query `SELECT filed_date as date, COUNT(*) AS filings FROM filings GROUP BY filed_date ORDER BY filed_date`.
- Ensure column aliasing produces `date` and `filings` columns so downstream plotting in `ui/dashboard.py` functions without modifications.

## Non-Goals

- Redesigning dashboard chart visualizations or altering other summary metrics in `ui/dashboard.py`.
- Adding scaffold-only stubs, mocks, or empty bypass functions without wiring up the real implementation does NOT count as done and constitutes a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update SQL query in function `load_delta()` in `ui/dashboard.py` to aggregate filing dates from `filings.filed_date` instead of table `holdings`.
- [ ] Add regression test in `tests/test_dashboard.py` asserting `load_delta()` executes without SQL syntax or column errors and returns grouped counts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `pytest tests/test_dashboard.py` executes without errors.
- Invoking `load_delta(engine)` against a seeded database returns a DataFrame containing `date` and `filings` columns.
- Verification gate: deliberately break the implementation by referencing `holdings.filed` in `ui/dashboard.py` and confirm `pytest tests/test_dashboard.py` fails with a database missing column error.
issues.title: fix(dashboard): resolve crash in load_delta on missing filed column
